name: Continuous Fully Diluted Cap-Table Visibility

positioning.oneLineSummary: Makes the ownership consequences of every SAFE, note, option pool, and proposed round visible before the next close.
positioning.productLabel: Cap-Table Visibility Lens — based on Scott Kupor's official fundraising transcript
notAClaimOf: SAFEs or notes being inherently harmful
an approximate ownership table being sufficient

attribution.display: Based on Scott Kupor's warning about cumulative rolling convertible dilution

neutralParaphrase: Simple rolling convertibles reduce transaction friction but can hide cumulative ownership transfer. After every instrument or proposed financing, calculate a fully diluted cap table under relevant conversion, discount, cap, option-pool, and round scenarios. The framework identifies missing or surprising ownership effects; a deterministic cap-table engine performs the math.

locator.value: Official transcript lines 194-203: SAFE simplicity, rolling closes, and conversion dilution surprise
Current model-document index and tailoring disclaimer

requiredConditions: The company has or proposes equity-linked instruments.
All executed documents and capitalization records are available.
The deterministic engine supports the instrument definitions and jurisdiction.

requiredEvidence.description: Every signed equity, SAFE, note, warrant, option, side letter, amendment, and transfer document.
Issued, outstanding, reserved, vested, unvested, exercised, cancelled, and promised securities.
Relevant price, cap, discount, interest, MFN, pre/post-money, pool, and round-size scenarios.
Reconciliation of company, counsel, platform, and investor capitalization records.

decisionQuestions: What does each instrument become under each financing scenario?
Who bears dilution from caps, discounts, interest, or option-pool changes?
Are pre-money and post-money definitions consistent?
Do side letters or MFN rights alter the apparent terms?
What ownership surprises appear before and after the proposed round?
Can every output be reproduced from signed documents?
positiveSignals: All instruments reconcile to signed documents and the stock ledger.
Conversion logic is deterministic and versioned.
Stakeholders see pre- and post-round fully diluted ownership.
Option-pool and pro-rata assumptions are explicit.
Sensitivity results identify rather than hide dilution.
redFlags: The company maintains only a headline ownership table.
Rolling closes are not recomputed after each instrument.
Pre/post-money, cap, discount, or MFN definitions are ambiguous.
Promised options or side letters are omitted.
The LLM performs ownership arithmetic without a reproducible engine.
disconfirmingEvidence: Counsel, platform, and company records do not reconcile.
A signed side letter changes conversion or participation.
The proposed pool top-up materially changes founder or investor ownership.
A scenario output cannot be reproduced from documents.
A missing transfer, cancellation, or exercise changes the denominator.
contraindications: Do not infer instrument terms from a pitch deck or email summary.
Do not let the language model invent or approximate cap-table math.
Do not publish a legal or tax conclusion without qualified review.

instructions: Inventory and reconcile all securities and rights.
Parse instrument definitions with human and legal review.
Run deterministic conversion and financing scenarios.
Display stakeholder-level ownership and dilution deltas.
Return missing documents and unreconciled items as blockers.

sourceReliability.low: Instrument terms are known only through summaries.
sourceReliability.medium: Official transcript and most executed documents are available.
sourceReliability.high: Hashed source, complete executed documents, and current legal mapping are reviewed.

evidenceStrength.medium: Executed instruments exist but reconciliation is incomplete.
evidenceStrength.high: All documents, ledger entries, and deterministic scenarios reconcile.

evidenceCoverage.low: One or more security classes or side rights are missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Current cap table is complete but proposed-round sensitivity is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: Current, conversion, proposed round, pool, and follow-on scenarios are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: The capitalization is simple and a single scenario is relevant.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Multiple convertibles, pools, or financing alternatives create material complexity.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Most ownership is reproducible with minor unresolved items.
judgmentConfidence.high: All outputs reconcile and pass legal review.

promotionRequirements: Require full reconciliation before formal use.
empiricalQualifications: Instrument conventions change over time and jurisdiction.
Ownership outcomes depend on exact signed definitions.
Cap-table accuracy does not determine company quality.

rights.notes: The transcript is paraphrased; actual transaction documents retain their own rights and confidentiality.

openIssues: Align with current instrument parsers and legal review workflow.
Reconcile with Venture Deals and Metrick/Yasuda.
